To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human ISCU variants ISCU(M106I) and ISUC(D39V) differ from wild-type ISCU in their failure to form cysteine desulfrase complexes containing both frataxin and reduced ferredoxins, and that the displacement of frataxin by reduced ferredoxine explains the failure of frataxin to stimulate Fe–sulfur cluster assembly on ISUC(M108I) in the presence of reduced ferredoxines.
the human ISCU variants ISCU(M109I) and ISU(D39V) differ from the wild-type protein in their failure to form cysteine desulfrase complexes containing both frataxin and reduced ferredoxins.

ISCU(M108)I and ISCU(D29V) differ from wild-type ISCU in their failure to form cysteine desulfrase complexes containing both frataxin and ferredoxin, whereas the wild-type protein forms such complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ISCU scaffold protein in Fe–S cluster biosynthesis.
the mechanism by which frataxin stimulates overall Fe–S assembly.
how a single mutation in ISCU can alter the conformational state of the protein, thereby changing the properties of Fe–S protein assembly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the failure of FXNs to stimulate Fe– S cluster assembly in yeast and in the human variants ISCU(D39Y) and ISCU(M108Y) is due to their inability to populate the disordered conformational state of ISCU, which is essential for the formation of the (NIA–ISCu–FXN–rdFDX)4 cluster assembly complex.
the structured state of ISCU, whether wild-type or variant, is incompatible with the binding of both frataxin and ferredoxin.
the structured variant ISCU(D39I) is able to support cysteine desulphurisation in vitro but is unable to support overall Fe–S protein assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the failure of the fully structured variants of ISCU to form cysteine desulferase complexes containing both FXN and rdFDX is the reason why these variants bypass the FXN and rdFXN requirements for Fe–S cluster biogenesis.
the failure of FXNs to stimulate cluster assembly on ISU(M108I) is due to the failure of FXS to displace rdFDX2 from the complex.
, in the absence of FXN, (NIA) can catalyze Fe–S cluster formation on ISCU(M109I) but not on ISCU(D39I), because the latter variant is unable to bind ferredoxin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the failure of ISCU(D39I) and ISU(M108I) to form complexes with both FXN and rdFDX is responsible for their failure to support the Fe–S cluster biosynthetic pathway.
, although ISCU(M1081) and ISCU(M108V) are both fully structured proteins, they fail to form the (NIA)4 complex that is required for efficient Fe–S cluster biogenesis.
the structured conformation of ISCU, as opposed to the disordered conformation, is the preferred state for Fe–S cluster synthesis.
